prov.heading: Credit Loss Expense
prov.text: A credit loss expense of $66 thousand was recognized for the three months ended September 30, 2026 as compared to a credit loss expense of $627 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2025. Net loan charge-offs for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $745 thousand compared to net loan recoveries of $344 thousand for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The credit loss expense in 2026 was primarily due to charge-offs in the commercial real estate and operating loan portfolios, partially offset by a decrease in specific reserves. The credit loss expense in 2025 was primarily due to an increase in specific reserves for loans in those same portfolios. The charge-offs in the third quarter of 2026 were on commercial real estate and operating loans for which specific reserves had previously been established.

nonint.text: Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $11.2 million compared to $10.2 million recorded for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 9.6%. The increase reflects higher professional fees, salaries and benefits. The increase in professional fees was primarily due to $600 thousand of consultant fees for certain contract negotiations during the three months ended September 30, 2026. The consultant fees are expected to continue throughout 2026 as negotiations are in process. The increase in salaries and benefits was driven by anticipated bonus payouts as Company performance thresholds are met, in addition to normal increases in salaries and benefits. The efficiency ratio was 54.97% for the third quarter of 2026 as compared to 61.76% in the third quarter of 2025. The efficiency ratio continues to improve as net interest margin increases.

nonop.text: Interest expense decreased $1.1 million, or 14.5%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 when compared to the same period in 2025. The lower interest expense for the period is primarily due to lower market rates and reduced borrowings.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text: Income tax expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $2.1 million compared to $1.2 million recorded for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The effective tax rate was 23% and 20% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The increase in income tax expense and effective tax rate was primarily due to higher net income and lower New Markets Tax Credits. The final year of tax credits was 2025 for a majority of the New Markets Tax Credit projects.

net.text: The Company had net income of $7.0 million, or $0.80 per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $4.6 million, or $0.51 per share, for the three months ended September 30, 2025. The Company had net income of $18.9 million, or $2.14 per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to net income of $12.5 million, or $1.41 per share, for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in earnings is primarily due to an increase in net interest income. Net interest income increased due to higher yields and average balances on investments, combined with a declining cost of funds driven by lower market rates and reduced borrowings.

ocf.text: Net cash provided by operating activities for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $16.9 million compared to $13.9 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase of $3 million in cash provided by operating activities was primarily due to higher net interest income.

Net interest income.heading: Net Interest Income
Net interest income.text:
For the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, the Company's net interest margin adjusted for tax exempt income was 3.38% and 2.83%, respectively. Net interest income, prior to the adjustment for tax-exempt income, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $17.0 million compared to $14.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025.

For the three months ended September 30, 2026, interest income increased $1.8 million, or 8.2%, when compared to the same period in 2025. The increase is primarily due to higher yield and average balances on the investment portfolio and improved yield on the loan portfolio. Interest income recognized on nonaccrual loans for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025 was approximately $171 thousand and $54 thousand, respectively.

Interest expense decreased $1.1 million, or 14.5%, for the three months ended September 30, 2026 when compared to the same period in 2025. The lower interest expense for the period is primarily due to lower market rates and reduced borrowings.

Noninterest income.heading: Noninterest Income and Expense
Noninterest income.text:
Noninterest income for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $3.5 million compared to $2.5 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 36.7%. The increase is primarily due to an increase in wealth management income and other noninterest income. The increase in wealth management income is primarily due to estate and trust fees earned from several estates that concluded administration during the quarter, as well as continued growth in assets under management. The increase in other noninterest income is primarily due to $235 thousand of insurance proceeds received in connection with storm-related property damage.

Noninterest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 totaled $11.2 million compared to $10.2 million recorded for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of 9.6%. The increase reflects higher professional fees, salaries and benefits. The increase in professional fees was primarily due to $600 thousand of consultant fees for certain contract negotiations during the three months ended September 30, 2026. The consultant fees are expected to continue throughout 2026 as negotiations are in process. The increase in salaries and benefits was driven by anticipated bonus payouts as Company performance thresholds are met, in addition to normal increases in salaries and benefits.

intro.text: Ames National Corporation (the "Company") is an Iowa corporation and bank holding company registered under the Bank Holding Company Act of 1956, as amended. The Company owns 100% of the stock of six bank subsidiaries consisting of one national bank and five state-chartered banks, as described below. All of the Company’s operations are conducted in the State of Iowa and primarily within the central, north-central and south-central Iowa counties of Boone, Clarke, Hancock, Marshall, Polk, Story, Taylor and Union where the Company’s banking subsidiaries are located. The Company does not engage in any material business activities apart from its ownership of its banking subsidiaries and the management of its own loan portfolios. The principal executive offices of the Company are located at 323 Sixth Street, Ames, Iowa 50010.
